marks.gloss_en: דומיא דרגל: as regel is liable whether or not the object's substance is destroyed, so shen is liable whether or not the substance is consumed
Eating obligates even where the object's substance is not consumed (לא מכליא קרנא) -- from its being written next to regel, which is indifferent to consumption
דומיא דשן: as shen is liable whether the owner sent the animal or it went of itself, so regel is liable when it went of itself
Trampling obligates even where the animal went of itself (אזלא ממילא), not only where its owner sent it -- from its being written next to shen, which is indifferent to sending
מאי שנא שן -- דיש הנאה להזיקו וממונך ושמירתו עליך; הני נמי -- so tolada deshen is like shen
מאי שנא רגל -- דהזיקו מצוי וממונך ושמירתו עליך; הני נמי -- so tolada deregel is like regel
the Rabbis have it as established: a ten-handbreadth pit causes death
bor's tolada: one's stone, knife or load left in the public domain that damaged (where he renounced ownership -- at rest and ownerless they are bor-like)
candidate: Rav Papa meant the tolados of shen (rubbing against a wall for pleasure, dirtying produce for pleasure)
candidate: Rav Papa meant the ordinary tolados of regel (damage with its body, its hair, its load, its bridle, its bell, in the course of walking)
candidate: Rav Papa meant the tolada of bor (the stone, knife and load left in the public domain)
